changes.before: Keep exactly the intended browser event subscription while a component is visible.
changes.after: Return cleanup from an Effect to undo the work it set up.

before: An effect synchronizes a component with something outside React, such as a browser event subscription.
Return a cleanup function from the effect to undo its setup. React calls it before replacing that effect and when removing the component.
A dependency array lists reactive values used by the effect. When a listed value changes, React cleans up the old subscription before setting up the new one.
If setup reads channel, include channel in the dependency array. An empty array would leave this subscription attached to its original channel.
In development, Strict Mode may run a setup, cleanup, setup cycle to reveal missing cleanup. Correct cleanup makes this safe; do not hide the problem by disabling it.
The exercise sends custom browser events using new Event(channel) and window.dispatchEvent. These are local signals, not network messages.
Complete the cleanup. Show the listener, send a signal, switch channels, and hide it. The old channel must stop responding after the switch, and no subscription should remain after hiding.
after: An event listener is a function the browser calls when a chosen event happens. An Effect can add a listener while a component is on the page.
Return a cleanup function from the Effect. React calls it before replacing that Effect and when removing the component. Cleanup should undo that setup's own work.
The dependency list names changing values read by the Effect. When a listed value changes, React cleans up the old connection before starting the new one.
If setup reads a `channel` prop, include channel in the list. Using `[]` would keep listening to the original channel even after the prop changes.
Strict Mode is a development check that can run setup, cleanup, then setup again. Correct cleanup makes this safe. Removing that check would hide the mistake instead of fixing it.
The exercise sends events with `new Event(channel)` and `window.dispatchEvent`. These are signals inside the browser, not messages sent over the internet.
Complete the listener cleanup. After changing channels, the old one must stop responding. After hiding the listener, its connection must be removed. Leave unrelated listeners alone.

before.question: An effect subscribes to channel A. The channel prop becomes B. What should cleanup remove?
choices: The subscription to A created by the old effect
Only the new subscription to B
Every event listener on the entire window
before.explanation: Each effect cleanup closes over its own setup values. It removes its old A subscription before the new effect subscribes to B, without touching unrelated listeners.

after.question: An Effect listened to channel A. The prop changes to B. What should the old cleanup remove?
choices: The A connection created by that setup.
after.explanation: Each cleanup remembers its own setup values, so the old one removes its A connection.

changes.before: The fixture starts hidden so checks can observe setup and removal. Dependencies are supplied correctly; learner focuses on cleanup. Real DOM lifecycle and listener identity are tested. Do not add effects for values that can be calculated during render.
changes.after: The listener starts hidden. Show it, switch channels, and hide it to check the full setup and cleanup path.

project.title: Clean up an effect
project.task: Keep the intended event listener only while its component is visible. Clean up the old listener when the channel changes.
project.done_when: The old channel stops responding after a switch. Hiding removes the listener without removing unrelated ones.
